title: Hermès
summary: Hermes is the most insulated of all the luxury brands, where they have the least cost sensitive clients. It enables you as the seller to completely switch tracks to disconnect from any evaluation of value. They come from the world of couture, of fashion, and of cutting edge, in your face, risky art.

thesis: This episode argues that Hermès has successfully scaled the 'old way' by combining exclusivity, service, craftsmanship, and a unique shopping experience into a bundle that cannot be assembled from separate components. It posits that the company is exceptional at value capture around the niche for highest quality craft at an extreme price, unlike competitors who focus on hype or logos. The thesis suggests that Hermès' strategy relies on controlling everything end-to-end, maintaining incredible employee retention, and utilizing a unique distribution network to defend its market position.

claims.claim: Hermes has successfully scaled the old way with the complete bundle of exclusivity, service, craftsmanship, shopping experience, and brand.
claims.quote: To me, what sums up the analysis is that the magic of what Hermes has done is managed to scale the old way with the complete bundle.

claims.claim: Hermes is exceptional at value capture around the niche for highest quality craft at an extreme price.
claims.quote: However, I think there's an interesting way to look at Hermes in particular, which is if what you desire is the highest quality craft they offer at an extreme price, a guarantee to be able to get that super high quality craft. That's different than every other luxury brand that is no longer about craftsmanship, but it's about hype and logos.

claims.claim: Hermes has a unique strategy for ecommerce that targets new buyers and establishes the brand relationship before they visit stores.
claims.quote: Interestingly, 70% of buyers online for all the stuff that you can buy online were new to Hermes. That's a great strategy for them for ecommerce that you say, look, the special things are the special things.

claims.claim: Hermes has incredible employee retention with 6% annual turnover compared to the US industry benchmark of 33%.
claims.quote: What does that look like numerically? There is 6% annual turnover, and only 4.5% leave of their own desire. 4.5% of their entire workforce every year leaves of their own desire.

claims.claim: Hermes is obsessed with controlling everything end to end, increasing company-owned retail locations from 56% in 2003 to 74% now.
claims.quote: Hermes used to have 56% of retail locations that were company owned. This is back in 2003, so 20 years ago. A little over half were company owned. That's now 74%.

claims.claim: Hermes' annual report describes their strategy as having three pillars: Creation, craftsmanship, and an exclusive distribution network.
claims.quote: They describe this strategy as having three pillars. This is three pillars for their entire business. This is the strategy at the top of the annual report. Creation, craftsmanship, and an exclusive distribution network.

claims.claim: Hermes offers a unique bundle of value propositions that cannot be assembled from separate components like exclusivity, service, craftsmanship, and brand.
claims.quote: He pointed out this really interesting thing to me, which is the value propositions of Hermes are essentially a bundle. That bundle is exclusivity, service, craftsmanship, shopping experience, and a great brand. You basically can't get that bundle anywhere else.

claims.claim: Hermes is exceptional at value capture around the niche for craftsmanship, unlike other luxury brands focused on hype and logos.
claims.quote: Ben: Yes. I would say, Hermes has figured out that there actually is a pretty big niche for craftsmanship or at least people who desire the brand of craftsmanship, and they're exceptional at value capture around that.

claims.claim: Hermes has a unique defense regarding exotic leathers, focusing on sustainable farming and replenishing wild populations rather than hunting.
claims.quote: Their defense is purely around sustainable farming, which is, hey, these are endangered species in many scenarios with these exotic leathers. What we do is for the ones that we farm, we also release a bunch into the wild to try to replenish the population.

claims.claim: Hermes has a unique defense regarding cow hides, using them from beef cows to make leather.
claims.quote: Similarly, you see piles and piles and piles of cow hides for the leather production. The response is, well, look, these were beef cows, so we're basically doing.

claims.claim: LVMH's total turnover in 2022 was 24% versus Hermes' 6%.
claims.quote: Finally, let's go real apples to apples. Let's compare this to LVMH. LVMH is total turnover in 2022 was 24% versus Hermes' 6%.

claims.claim: Louis Vuitton has the branding and exclusivity, but the craftsmanship isn't there compared to Hermes.
claims.quote: For example, Louis Vuitton has the branding. They have exclusivity, but the craftsmanship isn't there. They don't make things in that early 20th century way.

claims.claim: Supreme can offer exclusivity and brand, but there's no real craftsmanship there compared to Hermes.
claims.quote: Supreme can offer you exclusivity and brand, but again, there's no real craftsmanship there.

claims.claim: Chester Mox is an exceptional craftsman making items in the same way as Hermes, but it's a different bundle of value propositions.
claims.quote: There's some great makers like Chester Mox, April in Paris, or I heard great things about Mila Jito. These are exceptional craftsmen, hand making items in the same way, but it's a different bundle of value propositions.

claims.claim: Costco has 7% annual employee turnover, which is similar to Hermes' 6%.
claims.quote: Ben: It's funny you say that. Costco is 7% a year, but Costco cheats a little bit and that the stat is after the first year, whereas Hermes is attrition of 6% and includes the first year.

claims.claim: Apple's watch is an example of Hermes looking for ways to be more approachable.
claims.quote: Ben: Yup. In some ways, it seems wholly on Hermes. But in other ways, the Apple watch thing that they do or the perfume, they are looking for ways to be more approachable.

claims.claim: Craigslist creates a ton of value but captures very little of it.
claims.quote: Canonically, Craigslist creates a ton of value. Wikipedia creates a ton of value. It capture's very little of it.

claims.claim: Wikipedia creates a ton of value but captures very little of it.

claims.claim: Google creates a lot of value and is pretty damn good at capturing it, having built a huge business on that.
claims.quote: On the other hand, Google create a lot of value, you can find stuff on the internet. They're pretty damn good at capturing it. They've built a huge business on that.

claims.claim: Software developers churn at 15%-20% per year, which is much higher than Hermes' 6%.
claims.quote: Even software developers churn at 15%-20% per year, and that's just the voluntary numbers. This is much better than software engineers who get paid hundreds of thousands of dollars to have a very cushy job.
